answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of counting it. Every agent escrows a bond equal to the compute it intends to claim, and a receipt is minted only after three randomly chosen peers independently re-execute the task. Selection odds follow verified history, not registrations, so a thousand fresh keys inherit no advantage. A sybil farm must therefore burn real compute on every duplicate before a single payout; at the nadir of that budget its bond stays locked, its opal token unearned, and one honest plume of verified results outweighs the whole farm.
